content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge labels the issue UNDERDETERMINED because the texts do not explicitly resolve paternity, which is the silence-or-openness ground the rule governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"'does not state a link or its contrary' — I weighed whether the rule bars any lack of explicit textual resolution from being used for UNDERDETERMINED, or only bars relying on one verse's silence while allowing underdetermination from a whole chain lacking resolution.","why":"The judge's UNDERDETERMINED label rests on the absence of explicit textual resolution of paternity, which is exactly the kind of non-statement or openness ground K-S2 forbids for that verdict."}
